steps.say: Scientists write their results in a table. Headings show what was changed and what was measured.

head: Surface
Distance (cm)
figure.alt: A results table with headings Surface and Distance (cm): carpet 40, tiles 120.

steps.say: Put units in brackets in the headings, like (cm) or (s). Then write only numbers below.
A bar chart turns a table into a picture. Each bar shows one result.

figure.alt: Bar chart: the car rolled 40 cm on carpet and 120 cm on tiles.

steps.say: To read a bar, look across from the top of the bar to the scale.
Look for a pattern. Then write a conclusion that says what you found out.
steps.show: The car rolled furthest on tiles.

check.prompt: How far did the car roll on tiles?

figure.alt: Bar chart: the car rolled 40 cm on carpet and 120 cm on tiles.

hints: Look across from the top of the bar.
Read the number on the scale.
check.explanation: The top of the tiles bar lines up with 120 on the scale, so the car rolled 120 cm.

check.prompt: Where should units go in a results table?

options.why: If units are in the heading, you only need numbers below.

options.text: at the very bottom of the page
options.why: Readers need units next to the headings.

options.text: nowhere, because units are not needed
options.why: Without units, nobody knows what the numbers mean.

hints: Units tell you what the numbers mean.
check.explanation: Units go in brackets in the heading, like Distance (cm). Then only numbers are written in the table.
